parametric.claim: Index insurance pays out benefits on the basis of a predetermined index, such as rainfall level, without requiring the traditional services of insurance claims assessors.
parametric.source_title: Insurance (IFC Financial Inclusion page, includes FAQ: Index Insurance from the Global Index Insurance Facility)
parametric.publisher: International Finance Corporation (World Bank Group), Global Index Insurance Facility
parametric.quote: pays out benefits on the basis of a predetermined index (e.g. rainfall level) for loss of assets and investments, primarily working capital, resulting from weather and catastrophic events

parametric.claim: The index is set before the insurance period starts and tracks how far conditions such as rainfall or temperature move away from normal levels.
parametric.source_title: Insurance (IFC Financial Inclusion page, includes FAQ: Index Insurance from the Global Index Insurance Facility)
parametric.publisher: International Finance Corporation (World Bank Group), Global Index Insurance Facility
parametric.quote: Before the start of the insurance period, a statistical index is developed. The index measures deviations from the normal level of parameters such as rainfall, temperature

parametric.claim: Because index insurance does not necessarily require the traditional services of insurance claims assessors, claims can be settled faster and more objectively.
parametric.source_title: Insurance (IFC Financial Inclusion page, includes FAQ: Index Insurance from the Global Index Insurance Facility)
parametric.publisher: International Finance Corporation (World Bank Group), Global Index Insurance Facility
parametric.quote: Because index insurance does not necessarily require the traditional services of insurance claims assessors, it allows for the claims settlement processes to be quicker and more objective.

parametric.claim: In a traditional crop insurance contract, payouts follow a loss assessment made after the event, while an index contract uses a payout scale agreed in advance that sets how much is paid for each unit of the weather measure.
parametric.source_title: Weather Index Insurance for Agriculture: Guidance for Development Practitioners (Agriculture and Rural Development Discussion Paper 50)
parametric.quote: In a traditional contract, the insurer will price the contract based mainly on probabilistic models, and payouts will be made in accordance to an ex-post loss assessment. For indexbased contracts, however, it is necessary to agree to an ex-ante payout scale

parametric.claim: Removing field loss assessment cuts running costs, because traditional crop insurance has to send out large numbers of trained assessors.
parametric.source_title: Weather Index Insurance for Agriculture: Guidance for Development Practitioners (Agriculture and Rural Development Discussion Paper 50)
parametric.quote: The ability of index insurance to make payouts without field assessment clearly reduces administrative costs by eliminating the need for assessors.

parametric.claim: Because the payout depends on an independent weather measurement and not on what happens on the farm, farmers cannot influence the claim, which reduces moral hazard.
parametric.source_title: Weather Index Insurance for Agriculture: Guidance for Development Practitioners (Agriculture and Rural Development Discussion Paper 50)
parametric.quote: With index insurance, farmers have no ability or incentive to influence the claim, since payout is based on an independent and exogenous weather parameter, independent of farmers' behavior.

parametric.claim: All farmers in a defined area buy on the same terms and payout scale, which the World Bank says virtually eliminates adverse selection for insurers.
parametric.source_title: Weather Index Insurance for Agriculture: Guidance for Development Practitioners (Agriculture and Rural Development Discussion Paper 50)
parametric.quote: farmers subscribe based on the terms, conditions, and payout scale for all farmers in their defined area, virtually eliminating the adverse selection problem for insurers.

parametric.claim: The main trade-off is basis risk, the gap between what the index pays and what the farmer actually lost, and the World Bank calls it the most problematic feature of index insurance.
parametric.source_title: Weather Index Insurance for Agriculture: Guidance for Development Practitioners (Agriculture and Rural Development Discussion Paper 50)
parametric.quote: Basis risk is the most problematic feature of index insurance. It is the difference between the payout as measured by the index and the actual loss incurred by the farmer.

parametric.claim: Because the trigger matches losses only imperfectly, index insurance can pay in years when there are no losses and fail to pay in years when there are.
parametric.source_title: How to Measure Whether Index Insurance Provides Reliable Protection (Policy Research Working Paper 7744), by Karlijn Morsink, Daniel Jonathan Clarke and Shadreck Mapfumo
parametric.publisher: World Bank Group, Finance and Markets Global Practice
parametric.quote: index insurance provides claim payments based on a trigger that is only imperfectly correlated with losses. This implies that it carries basis risk: it may provide claim payments in years when there are no losses, and no claim payments in years when there are losses.

parametric.claim: Basis risk grows with the distance between the weather station or satellite measurement and the farm, so denser stations and finer satellite pixels help reduce it.
parametric.source_title: Insurance (IFC Financial Inclusion page, includes FAQ: Index Insurance from the Global Index Insurance Facility)
parametric.publisher: International Finance Corporation (World Bank Group), Global Index Insurance Facility
parametric.quote: The greater the distance between the measurement instrument and the field, the greater the basis risk. Some households that experience loss may not receive compensation while others that experience no loss may receive payments.

basis-risk.claim: Basis risk in index insurance is the chance that the index reading does not match the actual loss on a farmer's own field.
basis-risk.publisher: Global Index Insurance Facility (now Global Inclusive Insurance Facility), World Bank Group
basis-risk.quote: Basis risk in index insurance arises when the index measurements do not match an individual insured’s actual losses.

basis-risk.claim: Because payouts follow an index rather than an assessed loss, a policy can pay in a year with no losses and fail to pay in a year when farmers do lose crops.
basis-risk.source_title: How to Measure Whether Index Insurance Provides Reliable Protection (Policy Research Working Paper 7744), Morsink, Clarke and Mapfumo
basis-risk.publisher: World Bank Group, Finance and Markets Global Practice
basis-risk.quote: it may provide claim payments in years when there are no losses, and no claim payments in years when there are losses.

basis-risk.claim: Basis risk can never be fully removed, because an index built from rainfall, vegetation or area yields estimates the average loss in an area, not the loss of each farmer.
basis-risk.source_title: An Audit Rule to Protect Farmers in Case an Insurance Index Fails (Innovation Lab for Assets and Market Access Spotlight)
basis-risk.publisher: Feed the Future Innovation Lab for Assets and Market Access, UC Davis (USAID funded)
basis-risk.quote: An index of these factors predicts average losses in an area, not individual losses.

basis-risk.claim: In a study of index-based livestock insurance in northern Kenya, the index cut herders' exposure to large shared losses by an average of 62.8%, but the benefit was limited because many losses were specific to individual households.
basis-risk.source_title: Basis Risk and the Welfare Gains from Index Insurance: Evidence from Northern Kenya (MPRA Paper No. 59153), Jensen, Barrett and Mude
basis-risk.publisher: Cornell University and International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI), via Munich Personal RePEc Archive
basis-risk.quote: IBLI reduces exposure to covariate risk due to high loss events by an average of 62.8%. The benefits of reduced covariate risk exposure are relatively small, however, due to high exposure to seemingly mostly random idiosyncratic risk

basis-risk.claim: The same northern Kenya study found that, depending on the region, insured herders were still left with an average of 62.3% to 76.7% of their original risk from high loss events.
basis-risk.source_title: Basis Risk and the Welfare Gains from Index Insurance: Evidence from Northern Kenya (MPRA Paper No. 59153), Jensen, Barrett and Mude
basis-risk.publisher: Cornell University and International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI), via Munich Personal RePEc Archive
basis-risk.quote: Depending on covariate region, IBLI policy holders are left with an average of between 62.3% and 76.7% of their original risk due to high loss events.

basis-risk.claim: World Bank researchers warn that offering index insurance that does not reliably pay can damage the reputation of the donors, governments and companies behind it.
basis-risk.source_title: How to Measure Whether Index Insurance Provides Reliable Protection (Policy Research Working Paper 7744), Morsink, Clarke and Mapfumo
basis-risk.publisher: World Bank Group, Finance and Markets Global Practice
basis-risk.quote: Offering unreliable index insurance may lead to high reputation risk for donors, governments, and the private sector.

basis-risk.claim: Research in northern Kenya found that basis risk plays a major role in whether herders choose to buy index insurance at all.
basis-risk.source_title: How basis risk and spatiotemporal adverse selection influence demand for index insurance: Evidence from northern Kenya, Jensen, Mude and Barrett, Food Policy vol. 74
basis-risk.publisher: Food Policy (Elsevier), peer-reviewed; abstract on EconPapers
basis-risk.quote: our findings indicate that basis risk and spatiotemporal adverse selection also play a major role in determining demand for IBLI.

basis-risk.claim: Basis risk falls when each index area is uniform in weather and farming methods, and when there are more weather stations or satellite pixels covering the area.
basis-risk.publisher: Global Index Insurance Facility (now Global Inclusive Insurance Facility), World Bank Group
basis-risk.quote: This basis risk is reduced when the area covered by the index is homogeneous both in terms of weather and in terms of farming techniques. Therefore, as the density of weather stations and satellite pixels is increased basis, risk is minimized.

basis-risk.claim: An audit rule lets farmers report losses the index missed, and in a Tanzania pilot, if more than 30% of farmers complained, the insurer had to carry out an audit to check the index.
basis-risk.source_title: An Audit Rule to Protect Farmers in Case an Insurance Index Fails (Innovation Lab for Assets and Market Access Spotlight)
basis-risk.publisher: Feed the Future Innovation Lab for Assets and Market Access, UC Davis (USAID funded)
basis-risk.quote: If more than 30 percent of farmers registered a complaint, the company would be bound to carry out an audit for verification.

basis-risk.claim: Researchers recommend combining index insurance with stress-tolerant seed varieties and savings and credit products designed around risk, because insurance alone is likely to stay expensive.
basis-risk.source_title: Index Insurance for Developing Country Agriculture: A Reassessment, Carter, de Janvry, Sadoulet and Sarris, Annual Review of Resource Economics vol. 9
basis-risk.publisher: Annual Review of Resource Economics (Annual Reviews), peer-reviewed; abstract on EconPapers
basis-risk.quote: we suggest that improved index insurance be combined with stress tolerant seed varieties and new risk-oriented savings and credit products

wrsi.claim: The Water Requirement Satisfaction Index (WRSI) is an indicator of crop performance based on how much water was available to the crop during a growing season.
wrsi.source_title: CHIRPS - Croplands WRSI - Aug-Dec (product documentation: Water Requirement Satisfaction Index)
wrsi.quote: The spatially explicit water requirement satisfaction index (WRSI 1 ) is an indicator of crop performance based on the availability of water to the crop during a growing season.

wrsi.claim: WRSI is the ratio of the water a crop actually used over the season (actual evapotranspiration) to the water it needed (the crop water requirement), shown on a scale where 100 means no shortfall.
wrsi.source_title: CHIRPS - Croplands WRSI - Aug-Dec (product documentation: Water Requirement Satisfaction Index)
wrsi.quote: It is calculated as the ratio of seasonal actual evapotranspiration (AET) to the seasonal crop water requirement (WR) ... A case of 'no deficit' will result in a WRSI value of 100

wrsi.claim: The crop's water requirement is worked out from potential evapotranspiration, adjusted by a crop coefficient that changes with the crop's growth stage, and the model's two most important inputs are rainfall and potential evapotranspiration.
wrsi.source_title: CHIRPS - Croplands WRSI - Aug-Dec (product documentation: Water Requirement Satisfaction Index)
wrsi.quote: WR is calculated from the potential evapotranspiration (PET) using the crop coefficient (Kc) to adjust for the growth stage of the crop. ... The most important inputs to the model are precipitation and potential evapotranspiration (PET).

wrsi.claim: In the FEWS NET model, the season starts when at least 25 mm of rain falls in one 10-day period (dekad) and is followed by at least 20 mm in total over the next two dekads.
wrsi.source_title: CHIRPS - Croplands WRSI - Aug-Dec (product documentation: Water Requirement Satisfaction Index)
wrsi.quote: SOS is established when there is at least 25 mm of rainfall in one dekad followed by a total of at least 20 mm of rainfall in the next two consecutive decades.

wrsi.claim: FEWS NET treats a seasonal WRSI below 50 as a crop failure.
wrsi.source_title: CHIRPS - Croplands WRSI - Aug-Dec (product documentation: Water Requirement Satisfaction Index)
wrsi.quote: A seasonal WRSI value less than 50 is regarded as a crop failure condition (Smith, 1992).

wrsi.claim: WRSI was first developed by the UN Food and Agriculture Organization (FAO) and was later adapted and extended by the US Geological Survey for FEWS NET.
wrsi.source_title: CHIRPS - Croplands WRSI - Aug-Dec (product documentation: Water Requirement Satisfaction Index)
wrsi.quote: Originally developed by FAO, the WRSI has been adapted and extended by USGS

wrsi.claim: USGS scientists use WRSI to monitor crops, and a 2006 USGS fact sheet used WRSI maps to show that the 2000 drought badly affected maize growing areas of Kenya.
wrsi.source_title: Famine Early Warning System Network (FEWS NET), Fact Sheet 2006-3022
wrsi.quote: Drought conditions, which plagued much of the Horn of Africa in 2000, also severely affected maize growing regions of Kenya, as evidenced in these WRSI comparisons for 1999, long-term average, and 2000.

wrsi.claim: The African Risk Capacity, an African Union agency, uses WRSI in its Africa RiskView software, which underpins the parametric drought insurance it has offered to member states every year since 2014.
wrsi.quote: Africa RiskView uses the Water Requirements Satisfaction Index (WRSI) ... These national modelled drought response costs are the underlying basis for ARC's flagship parametric drought insurance products

wrsi.claim: CHIRPS (Climate Hazards Group InfraRed Precipitation with Station data) is a rainfall dataset from the Climate Hazards Center at UC Santa Barbara that combines satellite imagery with rain gauge data, covers 50 degrees south to 50 degrees north at 0.05 degree resolution, and runs from 1981 to near-present.
wrsi.source_title: CHIRPS: Rainfall Estimates from Rain Gauge and Satellite Observations
wrsi.publisher: Climate Hazards Center, UC Santa Barbara
wrsi.quote: Spanning 50°S-50°N (and all longitudes) and ranging from 1981 to near-present, CHIRPS2 incorporates our in-house climatology, CHPclim v1, 0.05° resolution satellite imagery, and in-situ station data

wrsi.claim: CHIRPS was built to support FEWS NET and was designed specifically for monitoring agricultural drought.
wrsi.source_title: The climate hazards infrared precipitation with stations: a new environmental record for monitoring extremes (Funk et al.)
wrsi.quote: CHIRPS was developed to support the United States Agency for International Development Famine Early Warning Systems Network (FEWS NET)

wrsi.claim: The Climate Hazards Center says production of CHIRPS version 2 will end after December 2026 and encourages users to move to CHIRPS version 3.
wrsi.source_title: CHIRPS: Rainfall Estimates from Rain Gauge and Satellite Observations
wrsi.publisher: Climate Hazards Center, UC Santa Barbara
wrsi.quote: Production of CHIRPS v2 will end after December 2026. Users are encouraged to transition to CHIRPS v3 to ensure continuity of operations.

kaip-subsidy.claim: Kenya's State Department for Agriculture presented its Area Yield Index Insurance experience at a disaster risk financing workshop in South Africa on 6 March 2024, in a talk by Kennedy Anahinga, Head of Crop Insurance.
kaip-subsidy.source_title: Area Yield Index Insurance Kenya Chapter (file name: Kenya AYII experience.pdf)
kaip-subsidy.publisher: State Department for Agriculture, Kenya (hosted by the Financial Protection Forum)
kaip-subsidy.quote: PRESENTATION MADE DURING DISASTER RISK FINANCING WORKSHOP HELD AT GLENBURN LODGE AND SPA SOUTH AFRICA ON 6TH MARCH, 2024 BY KENNEDY ANAHINGA HEAD: CROP INSURANCE; STATE DEPARTMENT FOR AGRICULTURE

kaip-subsidy.claim: Under Kenya's government-supported crop insurance programme, the government provides a 50% premium subsidy for farmers insuring between 0.5 and 20 acres of the insured crop.
kaip-subsidy.source_title: Area Yield Index Insurance Kenya Chapter (file name: Kenya AYII experience.pdf)
kaip-subsidy.publisher: State Department for Agriculture, Kenya (hosted by the Financial Protection Forum)
kaip-subsidy.quote: Provision of premium subsidy support of 50% on premiums paid by farmers for 0.5 to 20 acres of the insured crop.

kaip-subsidy.claim: In the presentation's worked maize example, a premium of 6% on a sum insured of KSh 41,080 came to KSh 2,464, and the government subsidy paid half of it, KSh 1,232.
kaip-subsidy.source_title: Area Yield Index Insurance Kenya Chapter (file name: Kenya AYII experience.pdf)
kaip-subsidy.publisher: State Department for Agriculture, Kenya (hosted by the Financial Protection Forum)
kaip-subsidy.quote: Sum assured = 1,643 X 25 = 41,080 Premium (6%) = 2,464 GoK subsidy (50%)= 1,232

kaip-subsidy.claim: The national government's State Department for Agriculture paid a total of US$3 million in crop insurance premium subsidies over the five years before the March 2024 presentation.
kaip-subsidy.source_title: Area Yield Index Insurance Kenya Chapter (file name: Kenya AYII experience.pdf)
kaip-subsidy.publisher: State Department for Agriculture, Kenya (hosted by the Financial Protection Forum)
kaip-subsidy.quote: In the last 5 years a total of US$ 3M has been paid in for subsidy support by the National Government GoK-SDA for farmers in crop insurance.

kaip-subsidy.claim: Area yield index insurance was piloted from 2016 to 2017, starting in three counties, and 1,000 farmers bought cover during the pilot; the Kenya Agricultural Insurance Programme (KAIP) was launched in 2018.
kaip-subsidy.source_title: Area Yield Index Insurance Kenya Chapter (file name: Kenya AYII experience.pdf)
kaip-subsidy.publisher: State Department for Agriculture, Kenya (hosted by the Financial Protection Forum)
kaip-subsidy.quote: Piloting 2016 to 2017 starting in 3 counties, 1,000 farmers procured cover for their crop. Launch of Kenya Agricultural Insurance Programme (KAIP) in 2018

kaip-subsidy.claim: The programme is run as a public-private partnership: the lead insurer of a pool of private insurers, at the time APA Insurance, receives farmers' premiums and the government subsidy on behalf of the pool, and the insurance regulator (IRA) approves the products developed by underwriters.
kaip-subsidy.source_title: Area Yield Index Insurance Kenya Chapter (file name: Kenya AYII experience.pdf)
kaip-subsidy.publisher: State Department for Agriculture, Kenya (hosted by the Financial Protection Forum)
kaip-subsidy.quote: The lead insurer receives premiums from the farmers and subsidy from the Government on behalf of the pool. Presently the lead insurer(APA insurance) manages the pool

kaip-subsidy.claim: By March 2024 the programme had reached 1.8 million farmers against a target of 5 million, and 42% of them were women.
kaip-subsidy.source_title: Area Yield Index Insurance Kenya Chapter (file name: Kenya AYII experience.pdf)
kaip-subsidy.publisher: State Department for Agriculture, Kenya (hosted by the Financial Protection Forum)
kaip-subsidy.quote: Farmers reached 1.8 million against a target of 5 Million. Of the 1.8 million farmers reached; 42 % were women.

kaip-subsidy.claim: According to the State Department for Agriculture, 55,000 farmers had received claim payments totalling US$2.5 million.
kaip-subsidy.source_title: Area Yield Index Insurance Kenya Chapter (file name: Kenya AYII experience.pdf)
kaip-subsidy.publisher: State Department for Agriculture, Kenya (hosted by the Financial Protection Forum)
kaip-subsidy.quote: 55,000 farmers have received claim compensation amounting to US$ 2.5M

kaip-subsidy.claim: Even so, the presentation says fewer than 0.5% of Kenya's smallholder farmers have crop insurance.
kaip-subsidy.source_title: Area Yield Index Insurance Kenya Chapter (file name: Kenya AYII experience.pdf)
kaip-subsidy.publisher: State Department for Agriculture, Kenya (hosted by the Financial Protection Forum)
kaip-subsidy.quote: Currently penetration of crop insurance among small holder farmers is still below 0.5% in Kenya.

kaip-subsidy.claim: A 2017 World Bank country profile described the early design of Kenya's area yield index insurance: the government provided a 50 percent premium subsidy for a maximum of five acres to farmers growing maize or wheat.
kaip-subsidy.source_title: Kenya (Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program country profile)
kaip-subsidy.publisher: World Bank Group, Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program
kaip-subsidy.quote: the government provides a 50 percent subsidy for a maximum of five acres to farmers growing maize or wheat.

livestock.claim: The Index-Based Livestock Insurance (IBLI) pilot was launched in January 2010 in Marsabit District in northern Kenya, and its contract used satellite measures of vegetation cover to predict average livestock deaths in local communities.
livestock.source_title: Coping with Drought: Assessing the Impacts of Livestock Insurance in Kenya (I4 Brief no. 2012-1), by Michael R. Carter and Sarah A. Janzen
livestock.publisher: Index Insurance Innovation Initiative (I4), BASIS / University of California, Davis (hosted on ILRI's CGSpace repository)
livestock.quote: In January 2010 the index-based livestock insurance (IBLI) pilot project was launched in Marsabit District of northern Kenya ... The IBLI index insurance contract uses satellite-based measures of vegetative cover to predict average livestock mortality experienced by local communities

livestock.claim: Under the IBLI pilot contract in Marsabit, households received a payout if predicted average livestock deaths reached 15%, and the first payouts were made in October and November 2011, averaging about 10,000 Kenyan shillings (roughly USD 150) per household in the study.
livestock.source_title: Coping with Drought: Assessing the Impacts of Livestock Insurance in Kenya (I4 Brief no. 2012-1), by Michael R. Carter and Sarah A. Janzen
livestock.publisher: Index Insurance Innovation Initiative (I4), BASIS / University of California, Davis (hosted on ILRI's CGSpace repository)
livestock.quote: Households receive a payout if the predicted average livestock mortality rate reaches 15%. In October-November 2011 the first IBLI payouts were made to households who had purchased insurance earlier in the year. Households in our study received an average payout of about 10,000 Kenyan Shillings (or roughly $150).

livestock.claim: After the 2011 payouts, IBLI led to a 22 percentage point drop in the share of households planning to eat fewer meals, and almost halved the share planning to sell more livestock to cope with the drought.
livestock.source_title: Coping with Drought: Assessing the Impacts of Livestock Insurance in Kenya (I4 Brief no. 2012-1), by Michael R. Carter and Sarah A. Janzen
livestock.publisher: Index Insurance Innovation Initiative (I4), BASIS / University of California, Davis (hosted on ILRI's CGSpace repository)
livestock.quote: IBLI results in a 22-percentage point drop in the number of households reducing the number of meals eaten as a coping strategy ... Similarly, there is almost a 50% reduction in the number of households who anticipated selling further livestock to cope with the wake of the 2011 drought.

livestock.claim: Index insurance leaves some risk uncovered: in Marsabit, IBLI covered only 62 to 77% of the herd mortality risk that households faced, mostly because losses vary from one household to the next.
livestock.source_title: The Favorable Impacts of Index-Based Livestock Insurance: Evaluation Results from Ethiopia and Kenya (I4 Brief 2015-03), by Nathan D. Jensen, Christopher B. Barrett and Andrew G. Mude
livestock.publisher: Index Insurance Innovation Initiative (I4) / BASIS, University of California, Davis
livestock.quote: In Marsabit, IBLI covers only 62-77% of the herd mortality risk that households face. ... A much larger portion of basis risk arises from between-household variation in livestock loss rates.

livestock.claim: During the 2011 drought in Marsabit, insured households were 36% less likely to expect to rely on distress sales of livestock and 25% less likely to expect to cut meals.
livestock.source_title: The Favorable Impacts of Index-Based Livestock Insurance: Evaluation Results from Ethiopia and Kenya (I4 Brief 2015-03), by Nathan D. Jensen, Christopher B. Barrett and Andrew G. Mude
livestock.publisher: Index Insurance Innovation Initiative (I4) / BASIS, University of California, Davis
livestock.quote: Insured households were 36% less likely to anticipate relying on distress sales of livestock and 25% less likely to foresee reducing meals to cope with the drought.

livestock.claim: KLIP uses the satellite Normalized Difference Vegetation Index (NDVI) to build an index of seasonal forage availability for each insured area, and a payout starts when the index falls below a set threshold and grows as forage scarcity gets worse.
livestock.source_title: Building financial resilience in pastoral communities in Africa: Lessons learned from implementing the Kenya Livestock Insurance Program (KLIP), by Francesco Fava, Nathaniel Jensen, James Sina, Andrew Mude and Barry Maher
livestock.publisher: World Bank Group (Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program) with the International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI)
livestock.source_date: No date printed on the pages read; data runs to the end of the 2020 long rains season
livestock.quote: NDVI time series are elaborated to obtain an area-aggregated index of relative seasonal forage availability ... When the index falls below a predefined threshold, a payout is triggered and increases proportionally to the severity of estimated forage scarcity.

livestock.claim: The product was redesigned from replacing dead animals to protecting live ones, so payouts now come at the start of a drought to help herders buy fodder, water and veterinary care.
livestock.source_title: Building financial resilience in pastoral communities in Africa: Lessons learned from implementing the Kenya Livestock Insurance Program (KLIP), by Francesco Fava, Nathaniel Jensen, James Sina, Andrew Mude and Barry Maher
livestock.publisher: World Bank Group (Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program) with the International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI)
livestock.source_date: No date printed on the pages read; data runs to the end of the 2020 long rains season
livestock.quote: the product was redesigned with a focus on 'asset protection'; payouts are provided at the onset of the drought during the rainy season to facilitate pastoralists implementing early coping and mitigation strategies (such as purchasing fodder/water/veterinary services

livestock.claim: KLIP began in October 2015 by buying fully subsidised cover for five tropical livestock units for each of 5,000 vulnerable households in Turkana and Wajir, then grew to eight counties and about 18,000 pastoralists a year.
livestock.source_title: Building financial resilience in pastoral communities in Africa: Lessons learned from implementing the Kenya Livestock Insurance Program (KLIP), by Francesco Fava, Nathaniel Jensen, James Sina, Andrew Mude and Barry Maher
livestock.publisher: World Bank Group (Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program) with the International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI)
livestock.source_date: No date printed on the pages read; data runs to the end of the 2020 long rains season
livestock.quote: KLIP started purchasing insurance coverage on behalf of 5,000 vulnerable households from two counties (Turkana and Wajir) in October 2015. Each household received fully subsidized coverage for five tropical livestock units (TLUs). KLIP rapidly scaled up to eight counties in the arid and semi-arid lands (ASALs) and to about 18,000 pastoralists annually.

livestock.claim: In the 2016-17 insurance year, KLIP covered six counties (14,010 households in the short rains season and 13,776 in the long rains season) and paid about USD 2.15 million for the short rains and USD 3.13 million for the long rains (about USD 5.3 million in total), against USD 1.64 million in premiums.
livestock.source_title: Building financial resilience in pastoral communities in Africa: Lessons learned from implementing the Kenya Livestock Insurance Program (KLIP), Table 1
livestock.publisher: World Bank Group (Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program) with the International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI)
livestock.source_date: No date printed on the pages read; data runs to the end of the 2020 long rains season
livestock.quote: Table 1: Summary of KLIP premiums, seasonal payouts, loss ratios, insured households, and TLUs ... 2016–17 Short rains 6 14,010 70,050 8.92 1.64 2.150 320.95 ... Long rains 6 13,776 68,880 3.130 ... Note: a. US$, million.

livestock.claim: By the end of the 2020 long rains season, the Government of Kenya had paid about USD 9.5 million in KLIP premiums and about USD 10 million had been paid out to beneficiaries.
livestock.source_title: Building financial resilience in pastoral communities in Africa: Lessons learned from implementing the Kenya Livestock Insurance Program (KLIP), by Francesco Fava, Nathaniel Jensen, James Sina, Andrew Mude and Barry Maher
livestock.publisher: World Bank Group (Disaster Risk Financing and Insurance Program) with the International Livestock Research Institute (ILRI)
livestock.source_date: No date printed on the pages read; data runs to the end of the 2020 long rains season
livestock.quote: As of end of LRLD 2020 season, the GoK has paid about US$9.5 million in premiums and a total of about US$10 million in payouts have been made to KLIP beneficiaries.

replanting.claim: ACRE Africa developed the Replanting Guarantee as a micro-insurance product that lets maize farmers re-invest in another bag of seed within the planting period if a lack of rain affects their crops.
replanting.source_title: Increasing smallholder uptake of seed insurance (case study)
replanting.publisher: Busara Center for Behavioral Economics, with ACRE Africa and FSD Kenya
replanting.source_date: Undated (no date printed on the PDF)
replanting.quote: RPG allows farmers to re-invest in another bag of Duma 43 Maize Seeds within the planting period should his/her crops be affected by a lack of rain.

replanting.claim: The registration card for the cover comes inside the seed pack, with instructions telling the farmer how to register.
replanting.source_title: Increasing smallholder uptake of seed insurance (case study)
replanting.publisher: Busara Center for Behavioral Economics, with ACRE Africa and FSD Kenya
replanting.source_date: Undated (no date printed on the PDF)
replanting.quote: The RPG insurance registration card is available inside the Duma 43 Maize Seeds pack, where a farmer is given instructions on how to register.

replanting.claim: In the version described in the Busara case study, if there is no rain for 21 days, ACRE automatically enables the farmer to purchase another packet of Duma 43 maize seed.
replanting.source_title: Increasing smallholder uptake of seed insurance (case study)
replanting.publisher: Busara Center for Behavioral Economics, with ACRE Africa and FSD Kenya
replanting.source_date: Undated (no date printed on the PDF)
replanting.quote: If there is no rain for 21 days, ACRE will automatically enable the farmer to purchase another packet of Duma 43 Maize Seeds.

replanting.claim: ACRE Africa describes the Replanting Guarantee as an index product: it watches the weather at each farmer's location and pays out when the weather index shows poor rainfall that forces replanting.
replanting.source_title: "The Insurance Works!" A story told by Jacinta Mutuse
replanting.publisher: Global Index Insurance Facility (blog post authored by ACRE Africa)
replanting.quote: The RPG covers the risk of poor rainfall that necessitates the replanting of crops. ... ACRE Africa monitors the weather at each farmer's location. An insurance payment is triggered if the weather index indicates the occurrence of adverse weather conditions

replanting.claim: In one case described by ACRE Africa, a Kenyan farmer received a Replanting Guarantee payout of about KES 900 (about 9 US dollars) on her phone through M-Pesa.
replanting.source_title: "The Insurance Works!" A story told by Jacinta Mutuse
replanting.publisher: Global Index Insurance Facility (blog post authored by ACRE Africa)
replanting.quote: Jacinta had just received about KES900 (US$9) through the Replanting Guarantee (RPG) Weather Index Insurance Product.

replanting.claim: ACRE uses satellite technology to geotag and monitor farms and uses Safaricom's M-Pesa to pay claims directly into farmers' mobile wallets. Farmers also have the option of an automatic discount on their next seed or fertilizer purchase.
replanting.source_title: ACRE Africa: Protecting Rural Africa Through Creative Partnerships and Technology
replanting.quote: The flagship product is the Replanting Guarantee (RPG) where each maize seed purchase from participating stores comes with insurance coverage. ... Farmers also have the option of receiving an automatic discount on the next seed/fertilizer purchase.

replanting.claim: The Replanting Guarantee was launched in 2013, and in 2016 it recorded over 100,000 registrations across Kenya's two rain seasons, which the 2017 African Insurance Awards entry calls 519 percent growth since launch.
replanting.source_title: African Insurance Awards 2017: nominee entry (Selin Konrat, Esther Kimani)
replanting.quote: In 2016, there were over 100,000 RPG registrations for the two rain seasons in Kenya. This was a 519% growth since the product had been launched in 2013.

replanting.claim: According to a 2015 Corporate Knights article citing Safaricom, more than 9,000 bags of seed were sold and more than 700 farmers were compensated under the replanting guarantee during the February to April 2014 planting season.
replanting.source_title: Climate-smart agriculture from the ground up
replanting.quote: more than 9,000 bags of seed were sold and more than 700 farmers compensated during the 2014 planting season from February through April

replanting.claim: ACRE worked with the Busara Center to find out why few buyers registered for the cover, and in tests that used social messages and a simpler process, registration rose by between 12 and 24 percent.
replanting.source_title: Increasing smallholder uptake of seed insurance (case study)
replanting.publisher: Busara Center for Behavioral Economics, with ACRE Africa and FSD Kenya
replanting.source_date: Undated (no date printed on the PDF)
replanting.quote: ACRE partnered with Busara to understand and test what was driving the low uptake of the RGP. ... Social framing and simplified processes increased registration rates between 12-24%

replanting.claim: The Replanting Guarantee starts as free cover that lasts until the end of germination and then serves as the entry point to ACRE Hakika, a paid weather-index extension product.
replanting.source_title: Formative evaluation of increasing uptake of ACRE Hakika
replanting.publisher: International Initiative for Impact Evaluation (3ie); authors Mercy Musya and Mercy Muttai, Busara Center
replanting.quote: The first introduction point to ACRE Hakika is Replanting Guarantee (RPG) ... the product that initially begins as a free insurance product until the end of the germination day, where it transitions into a paid extension product.

draft-regulations.claim: In 2025 Kenya's Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) published 13 draft regulations for the insurance sector, and one of them is the Insurance (Index Insurance) Regulations, 2025.
draft-regulations.source_title: Kenya: Proposed regulatory changes to insurance sector
draft-regulations.quote: The Insurance Regulatory Authority ( IRA ) has recently published a set of 13 draft regulations (Draft Regulations) that propose to amend existing regulations or create new regulatory frameworks for the insurance sector. These include: ... Insurance (Index Insurance) Regulations, 2025

draft-regulations.claim: The draft index insurance regulations aim to create a formal regulatory framework for index insurance in Kenya, a product class used so far mainly to cover risks in agriculture.
draft-regulations.source_title: Kenya: Proposed regulatory changes to insurance sector
draft-regulations.quote: the new Insurance (Index Insurance) Regulations, 2025, which aim to establish a formal regulatory framework for the provision of index insurance in Kenya. Index insurance is a growing product class in Kenya, particularly used so far to cover risks in the agricultural sector.

draft-regulations.claim: The draft would set out how the IRA approves index insurance products, the minimum features those products must have, and maximum claim payout periods.
draft-regulations.source_title: Kenya: Proposed regulatory changes to insurance sector
draft-regulations.quote: The Draft Regulations intend to establish the process for approval of such products by the IRA, their minimum features and maximum claim payout periods amongst others.

draft-regulations.claim: Business Daily reported that the draft says insurers must make index insurance payouts within ten days after the index has been triggered, and noted that Kenya currently sets no legal deadline for settling these claims.
draft-regulations.source_title: Kenya to cap 10-day payout rule in new climate insurance law
draft-regulations.quote: Currently, there is no legal timeframe within which insurers must settle such index-insurance risks. ... "An insurer shall make payouts within ten days after the index has been triggered," the draft states.

draft-regulations.claim: According to Business Daily, the draft would require IRA pre-approval for every index product and would let the IRA fine insurers that do not comply up to Sh1 million, cancel their licence or order them to take remedial action.
draft-regulations.source_title: Kenya to cap 10-day payout rule in new climate insurance law
draft-regulations.quote: The proposals will tighten oversight by requiring the pre-approval of the Insurance Regulatory Authority (IRA) for every index product. The rules also empower the IRA to impose penalties of up to Sh1 million on insurers who will fail to comply, or to cancel their licence or direct them to take remedial action.

draft-regulations.claim: Business Daily also reported that under the draft, insurers must keep basis risk low, file policy wording, pricing and an explanation of how the index was built, and use independent calculating agents vetted and recognised by the IRA.
draft-regulations.source_title: Kenya to cap 10-day payout rule in new climate insurance law
draft-regulations.quote: insurers must minimise "basis risk," which occurs when the data trigger does not perfectly match actual losses. Insurers will be required to submit detailed documentation, including policy wording, pricing and an explanation of how the index was developed. Independent calculating agents, who are responsible for computing triggers and payouts, will also be vetted and recognised by the IRA.

draft-regulations.claim: An article in the Association of Kenya Insurers journal says each policy would need a key features statement, could not be cancelled once cover began, and would include a dispute-resolution mechanism and a fallback payout formula for when the main index data is unavailable.
draft-regulations.source_title: The Insurer, Vol 33, December 2025: How legal support for agricultural insurance can drive Africa's sustainability (by Patrick Alushula)
draft-regulations.quote: insurers will be required to prepare a key features statement describing all policy terms, benefits, premiums and potential risks. The policies must be non-cancellable once coverage begins ... each policy will include a dispute-resolution mechanism and a fallback formula for calculating payouts in case the primary index data becomes unavailable

draft-regulations.claim: The regulations are still a draft. Once gazetted, they will give legal force to index-based insurance.
draft-regulations.source_title: The Insurer, Vol 33, December 2025: How legal support for agricultural insurance can drive Africa's sustainability (by Patrick Alushula)
draft-regulations.quote: Once gazetted, they will give legal force to index-based insurance

draft-regulations.claim: The IRA took public comments on the draft regulations until 21 November 2025, and at that point no timeline had been set for enacting them.
draft-regulations.source_title: Kenya: Proposed regulatory changes to insurance sector
draft-regulations.quote: The IRA is currently receiving comments from industry stakeholders and the public until 21 November 2025, following which the Draft Regulations may be amended to incorporate such input. At the moment, there is no timeline for their proposed enactment.

draft-regulations.claim: As of February 2026, EY described the Index Insurance Regulations 2025 as still a draft and said the IRA was still reviewing stakeholder submissions.
draft-regulations.source_title: Kenya's Insurance Regulatory Authority issues draft regulations: key changes and implications
draft-regulations.quote: Draft Insurance (Index Insurance) Regulations 2025: These regulations would establish the regulatory structure and define the IRA approval process for index insurance products, specifying minimum required features and limits on claim payout times. ... The IRA is still reviewing stakeholder submissions

glossary-sources.claim: A premium is the money charged for insurance cover, and it reflects the expected loss.
glossary-sources.quote: Money charged for the insurance coverage reflecting expectation of loss.

glossary-sources.claim: Index insurance pays claims based on an index that stands in for losses, not on an assessment of each policyholder's own losses.
glossary-sources.source_title: Weather Index Insurance for Agriculture: Guidance for Development Practitioners (Agriculture and Rural Development Discussion Paper 50), PDF page 28
glossary-sources.quote: Index insurance is a simplified form of insurance in which indemnity payments are based on values obtained from an index that serves as a proxy for losses rather than upon the assessed losses of each individual policyholder.

glossary-sources.claim: In index insurance the sum insured is usually based on the cost of production and fixed in the policy in advance, and payouts follow a scale set out in the policy.
glossary-sources.source_title: Weather Index Insurance for Agriculture: Guidance for Development Practitioners, PDF page 28
glossary-sources.quote: The sum insured is normally based on production cost on an agreed value basis (fixed in the policy in advance), and payouts are made based on a pre-established scale set out in the insurance policy

glossary-sources.claim: The trigger is the index level at which cover starts and a payout becomes due.
glossary-sources.source_title: Weather Index Insurance for Agriculture: Guidance for Development Practitioners, Annex, PDF page 98
glossary-sources.quote: The trigger level(s): The attachment level (or strike) at which the weather protection begins and financial compensation is received.

glossary-sources.claim: Basis risk is the gap between what the index pays and the loss the farmer actually suffers, so a payout can be higher or lower than the real loss.
glossary-sources.source_title: Weather Index Insurance for Agriculture: Guidance for Development Practitioners, PDF page 33
glossary-sources.quote: It is the difference between the payout as measured by the index and the actual loss incurred by the farmer.

glossary-sources.claim: NDVI (Normalized Difference Vegetation Index) is a satellite measure of green vegetation that always falls between minus one and plus one, where zero means no vegetation and values near plus one mean very dense green leaves.
glossary-sources.quote: A zero means no vegetation and close to +1 (0.8 - 0.9) indicates the highest possible density of green leaves.

glossary-sources.claim: A dekad splits each month into three parts: the 1st to the 10th, the 11th to the 20th, and the 21st to the last day, so the third dekad can be longer or shorter than 10 days.
glossary-sources.source_title: Weather Index Insurance for Agriculture: Guidance for Development Practitioners, Annex footnote 26, PDF page 100
glossary-sources.quote: A "dekad" is a conventional way of dividing a month in three intervals.

glossary-sources.claim: In FEWS NET crop water models, the onset of rains is used as a stand-in for the crop start of season, and a start dekad is confirmed only after three dekads.
glossary-sources.source_title: FEWS SOS, WRSI, and SWI Zip Products: Instruction and Explanation Document
glossary-sources.quote: Onset of Rains (SOS, surrogate for crop Start of Season)

glossary-sources.claim: Sales of index insurance must close before cover begins, so farmers cannot wait to see how the weather turns out before buying.
glossary-sources.source_title: Weather Index Insurance for Agriculture: Guidance for Development Practitioners, PDF page 61
glossary-sources.quote: The sales period for index insurance must close before the insurance coverage period actually begins.

glossary-sources.claim: A premium subsidy is the most common way governments support crop insurance, often paying about half the premium and up to 80 percent in some countries.
glossary-sources.source_title: Weather Index Insurance for Agriculture: Guidance for Development Practitioners, Box 2.1, PDF page 25 (printed page 12)
glossary-sources.quote: The most common government intervention is through premium subsidy, often around 50 percent of premium but up to 80 percent in some countries.

glossary-sources.claim: A reinsurer is an insurer that takes on risks from another insurer in return for a premium.
glossary-sources.quote: An insurer that assumes the risks of a ceding insurer in exchange for a premium.

glossary-sources.claim: A bordereau is a report an insurer sends to its reinsurer listing the individual risks it has insured under a reinsurance treaty.
glossary-sources.quote: information submitted by a cedant to a reinsurer giving details of individual risks insured under a reinsurance treaty
